title: Docker, Rails & Deployment
intro: Containerising a Rails application has several Rails-specific steps that don't apply to other frameworks: copying the Gemfile before the source code for Docker layer caching (so a code change doesn't invalidate the bundle install layer), running asset precompilation in the build stage (the production image doesn't need Node at runtime), setting RAILS_ENV=production, and ensuring the master key is available at runtime without being committed to the image. Kamal is the modern Rails deployment tool from the Rails team — it uses Docker under the hood with Traefik as the reverse proxy and supports zero-downtime deploys with a rolling restart strategy. This page covers the Dockerfile, Kamal deploy.yml, GitHub Actions for Rails CI/CD, and the zero-downtime migration patterns that must accompany every schema-changing deploy.
